assertions.name: n_target_equals_sum_of_cost
assertions.source: tr_M(beta_D) = sum_l y_l chi^l = sum_l t_l

assertions.name: uniform_rescale_factor_is_sqrt_of_shortfall
assertions.source: ceiling = max(t)*sum(t) is quadratic under t -> c*t

assertions.name: concentrated_cost_still_short
assertions.source: ceiling <= (sum t)^2, attained by concentrating on one block

assertions.name: required_trace_growth_factor
assertions.source: sum(t) >= sqrt(AME) even for a concentrated cost

assertions.name: no_negative_character_in_support
assertions.source: chi^lambda(beta_D) over the convention-D supported blocks

description: Quantifies the two escapes left after the level sweep. Corrects the cost figure: n_target = sum(t), so the ceiling is max(t)*sum(t), quadratic in the cost -- a uniform rescale needs 3.903x, not 15.23x. Even a perfectly concentrated cost at the current trace falls 6.72x short, so the constraint is on tr_M(beta_D) itself (2.59x larger). And every negative character sits in the convention-D kernel: the row cap zeroes exactly the blocks carrying the sign structure.
caveats: Scope (a). The sign observation locates WHERE the negative characters sit; it is not an argument that a program should occupy them, and it does not justify signed occupations. Nothing here claims a cost with a larger trace exists or is derivable, and nothing computes a binding contribution.

Supersedes the '15.23x on max(t)' figure reported earlier for the cost escape. That held n_target fixed, which is impossible since n_target = sum(t). The correct uniform-rescale factor is 3.903x, and reshaping at fixed total cannot close the gap at all.
